Routes._comment: Register/Login must stay anonymous at the gateway — there's no token to present yet.

Brute-force protection on this route is applied in Program.cs via ASP.NET Core's own RateLimiter, partitioned by client IP — NOT via Ocelot's RateLimitOptions. Ocelot's rate limiter identifies a 'client' by a self-declared request header, which an attacker mounting a credential-stuffing attack would simply omit or vary; it's meant for per-tenant/API-key throttling, not abuse protection. See the A3 writeup for how this was actually discovered (it silently failed with 503s in testing).
AuthenticationOptions is what makes Ocelot itself validate the JWT before proxying — an invalid/missing/expired token never reaches Identity.API at all.
